AuthStatusResponse.description:
Response for GET /api/auth/status.

``connected`` is true ONLY for the tenant's own live grant. A tenant served by
the platform channel is ``status="platform_default"`` with ``connected=false``
(``can_publish=true``); a tenant whose grant Google refused is
``status="reconnect_required"`` (``can_publish=false``).

can_publish.description: Whether an upload for this tenant would be attempted (own grant, or the operator-enabled platform channel)
can_publish.title: Can Publish

connected.description: True only when the tenant's OWN grant is live
connected.title: Connected

mode.description: Which resolution branch an upload takes: the tenant's own grant, the platform channel, or none (uploads fail with 'connect YouTube')
mode.title: Mode

needs_reconnect.description: mode=tenant only: the grant is unusable (refused by Google, or issued by an OAuth client the tenant no longer has); uploads fail until reconnect
needs_reconnect.title: Needs Reconnect

post.description:
Start the OAuth2 flow. Returns a Google consent URL for the tenant.

The one-time ``state`` is bound to ``tenant_id`` — the OWNER tenant — so the
public callback stores the grant under the tenant whose uploads will use it —
and to the OAuth client that starts the flow (the tenant's own client when
configured, else the platform client), so the callback exchanges the code
with that same client and records it on the grant.
post.summary: Start the OAuth2 flow — returns a Google consent URL

post.description:
Create an upload job and return immediately with a job_id for polling.

A render that is already on YouTube for this tenant is a **409**, not a
second upload. This route is the only entry point to the upload path (there
is no automatic retry anywhere in the service), so a repeat request is a
human re-submitting — usually after reading a job the reaper marked
``failed``, which is not evidence that nothing was published. The 409 names
the existing video so the operator can check the channel.
post.summary: Create a YouTube upload job — returns immediately with a job_id

get.summary: Poll the status of a specific YouTube upload job

post.description:
Raise the job's YouTube video to ``unlisted``/``public``. Never deletes, never lowers.

Called by the governed ``marketing.publish_video`` release of a video uploaded private.
404: no such job for this owner. 409: the job never published a video.
503: no channel credentials. 502: YouTube refused or no longer has the video.
post.summary: Release a private upload: set its YouTube video to unlisted or public

post.description:
Set the job's YouTube video to ``private``. Only ever reduces visibility.

404: no such job for this owner. 409: the job never published a video.
503: no channel credentials. 502: YouTube refused or no longer has the video.
post.summary: Retract a published upload: set its YouTube video to private (reversible)
